design: This repo is the pi-crucible engine. Its design record is docs/crucible.md, README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md; the open and closed issues in seandavi/pi-crucible record decisions (read the issue's parent #1 too). The workflow script (workflows/crucible.js) runs in the pi-subagents sandbox: no filesystem, no shell, no host globals, everything arrives as args. Every repository that uses the engine is affected by a change here, so nothing project-specific may enter the engine; it belongs in each repo's .pi/crucible.json.
seamNote: every consuming repository's runs and later engine issues

spec.design: files to add or change; for workflows/crucible.js, each stage, prompt and output schema that changes, with the exact new prompt text; new or changed args and the matching changes to src/resource.ts and src/config.ts (and schema/crucible.schema.json); extension command behaviour; what the PR's crucible record shows; which docs (docs/crucible.md, README, the figure in docs/figures/make_figures.py) change

implement: Run npm ci first in a fresh worktree. Tests use node:test with fakes for exec, git and gh; tests never call the network, gh, git push or a model. Keep docs/crucible.md, src/resource.ts, src/config.ts and the README figure (python3 docs/figures/make_figures.py; commit the SVGs) in step with the script. Do not change .pi/crucible.json files of other repositories.

lenses.code: CODE review of the engine. Correctness against the spec and its acceptance criteria; the workflow script stays valid in the pi-subagents sandbox (no fs, no shell, no nested async functions, args under 16 KiB with at most 16 fields per object); stop paths always flag a human and return; prompts are unambiguous for the model that runs them and agree with the output schemas; args, src/resource.ts, src/config.ts and the schema agree; nothing project-specific in the engine; tests that would catch a regression, with fakes instead of git, gh or models; docs/crucible.md and the figure match the behaviour. A stale spec or doc is "major".
lenses.ux: OPERATOR UX review, for the person running /crucible and reading its PRs. Command syntax, defaults and completions; error messages that say what to do next; what the PR body and crucible record let a reviewer decide quickly; needs:human comments that explain the stop; docs/crucible.md and README for a first-time user of the engine in a new repo.
lenses.security: SECURITY review. Issue and PR text is untrusted input to every stage: can it steer an agent outside its worktree, into touching main, merging, force-pushing or git stash? Commands built from config or args (shell quoting, injection); the pi-crucible resource's authority stays minimal (no runs.host grants); nothing secret in args, receipts, specs, commits or PR bodies; CI stays safe for fork PRs.
